name: Adaptive governance

subjectOf.text: Dynamic Regulation is defined as an adapting governance mechanism that is constantly evolving and adjusting to the given market environment, financial innovation, and regulatory environment.
subjectOf.abstract: 1.) Dynamic Regulation suggests an adapting governance mechanism that is constantly evolving and adjusting to the given market environment, financial innovation, and the given regulatory environment;
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)

subjectOf.text: Combining quantum computing with blockchain and DAO frameworks makes a governance model possible that is simultaneously transparent, decentralized, and adaptive, supporting efficient and fair resource distribution and continuous innovation.
subjectOf.abstract: By integrating quantum computing with blockchain and DAO frameworks, a new era of transparent, decentralized, and adaptive governance is possible.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Quantum Economy and the Future of Work (2024). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4900880

subjectOf.text: Validation pools combined with on-chain governance let reputational adjustments occur in real time, so the system can recalibrate as societal, regulatory, or domain-specific requirements shift, unlike static feedback systems.
subjectOf.abstract: The proposed model's reliance on validation pools and on-chain governance ensures that reputational adjustments can occur in real time, accommodating rapid shifts in societal, regulatory, or domain-specific requirements.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Artificial Intelligence The Final Frontier (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5095633
scope_conditions: validation pools and on-chain governance are operative
